assertions.title: Narrative labels stripped

steps.action: Open the shared dashboard and inspect visible panel titles, status copy, and control labels.
steps.expected: User-facing labels are neutral and technical throughout the dashboard.
steps.observed: The dashboard rendered, but visible labels still included 'witness thread', 'Presence Operating Rail', 'Fork Tax Canticle', 'Receipt River', and 'galaxy sweep'.

steps.action: Compare renamed headings with the rest of the visible UI.
steps.expected: All panels/tooltips/buttons/status text should match the neutral naming cleanup.
steps.observed: Some headings were neutralized (for example 'Simulation Viewport' and 'Agent Creator'), but multiple visible cards and status lines still carried narrative terminology.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed via agent-browser errors during load and inspection
evidence.network: Tracked repeated GET requests to http://127.0.0.1:9787/api/simulation?perspective=hybrid&payload=trimmed and http://127.0.0.1:9787/api/agent/threat-radar/report?window_ticks=1440&limit=16.

assertions.issues: Visible narrative residue remains in panel labels and status copy, so the UI text cleanup is incomplete.

steps.action: Capture a full-page screenshot of the rendered dashboard.
steps.expected: The app should present as a clean dark dashboard with solid dark surfaces and no mystical/cosmic effects.
steps.observed: The dashboard rendered on solid dark navy/black panels and background surfaces, with no obvious glass, parallax, or cosmic backdrop effects visible in the page render.

steps.action: Visually inspect contrast and overall theme consistency across the visible layout.
steps.expected: The overall appearance should be professionally dark and readable.
steps.observed: The overall theme reads as a dark technical dashboard with generally adequate contrast, even though the content density is high.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed via agent-browser errors during load and inspection
evidence.network: Same tracked 9787 API requests were observed during the render, without uncaught JavaScript errors.

assertions.title: All panels visible and functional

steps.action: Inspect all visible dashboard panes, sidebars, and card stacks after initial load.
steps.expected: All visible panels render with readable content and appear usable from the user perspective.
steps.observed: All major panels mounted, but several lanes were extremely narrow with cramped/clipped text, and the Threat Radar card displayed 'Failed to fetch'.

steps.action: Check for browser-side rendering failures while reviewing the layout.
steps.expected: Panels should stay stable without rendering errors or broken UI sections.
steps.observed: No uncaught JavaScript errors were reported, but the degraded panel readability means the dashboard does not fully meet the visible/functional expectation.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed via agent-browser errors during load and inspection
evidence.network: Visible frontend traffic targeted the 9787 API endpoints noted above; the page remained mounted while the Threat Radar panel showed a failed-fetch state.

assertions.issues: The UI stays mounted, but multiple panels are visually degraded by the compressed layout and at least one visible card is already in a failed-fetch state.

frictions.description: The shared frontend rendered while polling API endpoints on port 9787, and one visible card entered a failed-fetch state even though the milestone notes already warned that backend-connected data might not be reliable.
frictions.resolution: Kept the assessment scoped to frontend render quality, visible text, panel availability, and absence of uncaught JavaScript errors.

summary: Tested 3 browser UI assertions on the shared Vite dashboard: 1 passed (VAL-UI-007) and 2 failed (VAL-UI-006, VAL-UI-008). The app rendered successfully in the browser and no uncaught JavaScript errors were observed during inspection.
